{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "The lighthouse at Skarvnes went automatic the winter Margit turned seventy, and after that nobody had any reason to climb the hill except her. She climbed it anyway, most mornings, because her knees had learned the path before they learned anything else and it seemed cruel to unteach them now.

The light still turned. That was the strange part. Some machine in Bergen told it when to wake and when to sleep, and it obeyed without ever having seen the sea it warned about. Margit found this both admirable and a little sad, the way she found most things that worked without needing her.

There were nine houses in the cove and four of them had lights in the evening. The others held their breath. Summer people came in July and opened the windows and said how quiet it was, as if quiet were something they had discovered rather than something that had waited for them to leave.

Her son called on Thursdays. He asked about the weather because the weather was safe. She told him the truth, which was that it was doing what it always did, and that she had stopped expecting otherwise.

What she did not say was that the hill had begun to feel like company. The wind on the north face, the particular groan of the iron door, the gulls who had decided she was harmless. None of it needed her. All of it noticed her.

She thought that might be enough, and found, most mornings, that it was."}
